sources.entry: Papr - RSS reader with adjustable typography, keyboard-driven navigation, and highlight export to Readwise, Notion and Obsidian. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/l0ng-ai/papr) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Papr is a fast, native, local-first RSS reader for desktop, paired with a command-line tool (`papr`) designed for AI agents to read and triage feeds from the shell.
summary.what_it_does: The desktop app manages feeds and folders with OPML import/export, and offers smart views (All, Unread, Starred, Read Later) with live counts. It supports color-coded tags and rules that tag new articles automatically, and can fetch full article text when a feed only ships a summary. Optional AI features (summaries, article Q&A, digests) use a user-supplied API key, and a built-in audio player follows along from article to article. Read state can sync with a FreshRSS server. The `papr` CLI shares the same local database through the `papr-core` crate and provides commands to read, search, mark, extract, refresh, manage subscriptions, and sync with FreshRSS or Miniflux. Running bare `papr` prints an unread dashboard with suggested next commands, and output uses the TOON format.
use_cases: Read RSS feeds on a Mac, Windows, or Linux desktop
Let an AI agent like Claude Code or Codex triage feeds
Search and read full text of subscribed articles from the terminal
Sync read state with a FreshRSS or Miniflux server
Export highlights to Readwise, Notion, or Obsidian
Import or export feed subscriptions via OPML
notable: Desktop app and agent CLI share one local database via the papr-core crate
Bare `papr` prints an unread dashboard plus suggested next commands for agents
Bundled papr-rss skill loads on demand for agent feed tasks
Papr setup installs an ambient SessionStart hook for Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode
Localized in English, Japanese, and Simplified Chinese
caveats: AI features require the user's own API key
Full CLI command reference and install options are in a separate docs/cli.md file, not the README
Install instructions shown cover macOS, Windows, and Linux packages; the README lists no other platforms
keywords: triage my feeds with an ai
